final.executive_summary: Underweight AAPL and rebalance at the next session open to 1.5% of total equity, trimming roughly 3.0 shares (~$950 notional, ~$1 in fees) from 7.85 shares and leaving about 4.8 shares. This is a partial reduction, not an exit: the franchise and rising 200-day remain intact, but the tape, failed 320.28 reclaim, unfilled 310.69-329.59 gap, and corroborated 08-20 margin/guidance read-through skew near-term risk lower. Treat 305.59 as a warning level, not a hard stop; reassess toward 0.75% or flat only on a weekly close below 300.57 or a daily close below 302 on >60M shares with fresh momentum deterioration, and re-add only above 314.34 on >60M shares with MACD > -1.19 and RSI >55. Horizon 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY2026 print.
final.investment_thesis: The decisive evidence is the tape plus forward risk, not a broken franchise. AAPL closed at 309.35 below the 10 EMA (310.35), 50 SMA (310.21), and Bollinger midline (314.34), with MACD at -1.574 below its -1.194 signal. The 07-31 10-Q session gapped -7.36% to 308.91 on 132.5M shares (~2.5x normal) and has not recovered; the 08-20 tag of 320.28 closed at 311.30 and 08-21 closed near the session low, a failed reclaim and lower high beneath the unfilled 310.69-329.59 gap. RSI at 47.28 is not oversold and offers no springboard. Near-term asymmetry is negatively skewed: ~9% to the 200-day at 281.50 versus ~6.5% to a full gap fill, with the 305.59 intermediate level only ~1.2% below spot. The forward news set is corroborated: two independent 08-20 items flag slower growth and memory-cost margin pressure, while operating margin compressed sequentially from 34.02% in H1 to 32.62% in Q3 even as gross margin set a 50.06% record; R&D grew 32.5% against 16.1% revenue growth. The buyback cut to a 67% payout and only -1.1% net share reduction also thin the EPS-accretion leg. Against that, the bull case is real: nine-month revenue +16.1% to $364.4B, FCF +52.5% to $110.2B, net cash nearly doubled to $62.2B with no new term debt, and a rising 200-day at 281.50 with price ~9.9% above it. That is why this is a trim to 1.5%, not a liquidation. The risk debate converges on reduction; the disagreement is sizing. The conservative 1.0% target is too cosmetic: the difference between 1.0% and 1.5% is only ~$500 of exposure, and a repeat 07-31 gap would cost ~0.11% of total equity at 1.5% versus ~0.07% at 1.0%. The aggressive 3-4% re-add ladder is rejected: buying a 312.40/314.34 print inside the lower gap beneath the 316.3-320.3 supply shelf with invalidation near 305.59 is not convex. The neutral 1.5% construction wins, with the conservative correction adopted: 312.40 is a re-add gate, not a stop, and 305.59 is a warning rather than a forced exit because it is only ~0.49 ATR below spot. Prior lessons support the distinction: earlier AAPL Underweights that trimmed on momentum decay alone bled alpha, while the calls that worked were anchored to a real distribution print, which is present here. The 08-20 add to 2.50% is only partially unwound, not reversed. What would change the call: a volume-confirmed reclaim of 314.34 with MACD > -1.19 and RSI >55 would justify stepping back toward 2.0%, with at most 2.5% on a volume-confirmed close above 320.28; a weekly close below 300.57 or a daily close below 302 on >60M shares with fresh MACD/RSI deterioration would cut toward 0.75% or flat. No adds inside the 309-311 collision zone and no new capital ahead of the late-October Q4 print. Stated gaps: no valuation multiples, no consensus forward estimates, no options/positioning data, no segment or geographic mix, and the news set is headline-only (20 of 90 records) with an 08-14 to 08-18 blind spot.
final.time_horizon: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY2026 print
